title: The day he died
hook: 'Umar refused to believe it. Abu Bakr walked in, kissed his face, and steadied a whole community with one sentence.
glossary: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un

screens.text: **'Umar refused to believe it.** Then Abu Bakr walked in, kissed his face, and steadied a whole community with one sentence. This is a tender episode. Take it slowly.

**In Aisha's house.** The Prophet ﷺ died on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal, 11 AH, at sixty-three [Bukhari 1387; Muslim 2348; IslamQA 11575]. He was in Aisha's home, resting against her chest [Bukhari 4449].
bubbles: Near the end, she saw him looking at a toothstick, a siwak. She softened it for him, and he used it [Bukhari 4449].

cards.back: He died in her home, resting against her. She stayed with him to the end [Bukhari 4449].
In shock, he stood up and insisted the Prophet ﷺ had not died [Bukhari 3668].
He kissed his friend's face, then went out to steady the people. Keep going [Bukhari 3668].

screens.text: **His last words.** He dipped his hand in water, wiped his face, and said there is no god but Allah [Bukhari 4449]. Then he looked upward and said: with the highest companions [Bukhari 4463].
bubbles: He used to say that no prophet dies before being shown his place in Paradise and given the choice [Bukhari 4463]. Aisha understood: he had chosen.

screens.text: Sixty-three years, from Makkah to Madinah.

events.title: He dies
events.text: In Rabi' al-Awwal, at sixty-three, in Aisha's home [Bukhari 1387; Muslim 2348; Bukhari 4449].

events.title: Abu Bakr's words
events.text: Allah is alive and never dies [Bukhari 3668].

events.title: Buried where he died
events.text: In Aisha's house, now within his masjid in Madinah [IslamQA 11575; Yaqeen].

screens.text: **One sentence.** Abu Bakr uncovered his face and kissed him. Then he went out to the people: whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died; whoever worshipped Allah, Allah is alive and never dies [Bukhari 3668].
bubbles: Then he recited: *"Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him"* [Q 3:144, Saheeh Intl.]. And the people wept [Bukhari 3668].

screens.after: . [Other] messengers have passed on before him" [Q 3:144]

options.feedback: Yes. A beloved messenger and a human being. Only Allah is alive and never dies.
Not quite. He was a human being and Allah's messenger. Abu Bakr's point exactly [Bukhari 3668].
Not quite. Not a king: a messenger, like the messengers before him [Q 3:144].

screens.text: **He was human. Allah is alive.** Day 15 called him a human, not a god. On the hardest day, Abu Bakr lived that out. Grief is real too: his Companions wept. If you're grieving, you're allowed to.
bubbles: In loss, Muslims say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un: *"Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return"* [Q 2:156, Saheeh Intl.].

screens.situation: The imam who helped Marcus become Muslim is moving to another state. Marcus feels like his faith is leaving with him. He's thinking of not going back to the masjid.

options.text: Remember he became Muslim for Allah, keep in touch with the imam, and keep going to the masjid
options.feedback: Yes. People we love move on or pass away. Allah is always there. That was Abu Bakr's point.

options.text: Stop going; it won't be the same
options.feedback: Not quite. The masjid is still Allah's house, and new people will come into his life.

options.text: Decide his faith was never real if it depends on one person
options.feedback: Not quite. Missing a teacher is natural. His faith is in Allah, who never leaves.

screens.text: He was a human being, and he died. Allah is alive and never dies. That's where Muslims rest their hearts.
Next episode: his family. A father of four daughters, a grieving parent, and a grandfather who kissed his grandsons in public.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- He died on a Monday [Bukhari 1387] in Rabi' al-Awwal, 11 AH [IslamQA 11575], 632 CE [Yaqeen, *What Islam Says About Prophet Muhammad*], aged sixty-three [Muslim 2348; Bukhari 3902]. The day of the month is disputed: 12 Rabi' al-Awwal is the best-known view [IslamQA 147601; Yaqeen], but others exist, so the screens say only "in Rabi' al-Awwal".
- He died in Aisha's house, on her day, leaning against her chest; she softened a siwak for him and he used it; he wiped his face with water saying there is no god but Allah, and that death has its agonies; he raised his hand, asking to be with the highest companion, until his hand fell [Bukhari 4449]. He used to say no prophet dies until shown his place in Paradise and given the choice; at the end he looked at the ceiling and said, O Allah, with the highest companions; Aisha understood he had chosen [Bukhari 4463].
- 'Umar, in shock, said he had not died. Abu Bakr came, uncovered and kissed him, and said he was good in life and death; then told the people whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died, and whoever worshipped Allah, Allah is alive and never dies; he recited Q 39:30 ("Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die") and Q 3:144; the people wept [Bukhari 3668].
- He was buried where he died, in Aisha's house, now within the Prophet's Masjid [IslamQA 11575; Yaqeen].
- Day 15 teaches "a human, not a god"; Day 77 covers grief; Day 41 the afterlife.

**Likely questions**
- *"Where is he buried? Can I visit?"* In Madinah, in what was Aisha's house, now inside the Prophet's Masjid. Visiting the masjid is beloved to Muslims; questions about how to visit the grave go to the imam.
- *"What does 'with the highest companions' mean?"* Scholars explain it as the company of the prophets and the righteous with Allah; Aisha understood he was choosing to go [Bukhari 4463].
- *"Is he alive in his grave? Does he hear us?"* Keep to the episode: he died, as Abu Bakr said [Bukhari 3668; Q 39:30]. Questions about the life of the grave or intercession go to the imam; don't take sides between Muslim groups.
- *"Why didn't 'Umar believe it?"* Grief and shock; he later said nothing else had occurred to him [Bukhari 3668]. Even great believers are shaken by loss.
- *"Who led after him?"* Succession politics are outside this track; say briefly that the Muslims pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr [Bukhari 3668] and suggest the imam for more.
- *"I'm grieving someone."* Listen first; tears are mercy [Bukhari 1303]; "To Him we will return" [Q 2:155–157]; Day 77. If the person who died wasn't Muslim, follow Day 77: comfort first, no comment on anyone's fate, offer the imam. (scholar question Q23)

**Escalate:** a convert's deceased non-Muslim relative (Q23); grief that sounds like crisis (mentor; safety rule); questions about the grave, intercession or the Mawlid (imam).

**Don't**
- Don't give 12 Rabi' al-Awwal as fact or discuss celebrating the Mawlid.
- Don't discuss Saqifah or succession disputes.
- Don't describe his death agonies in detail on your own initiative.
